name: Rowan Jimenez
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember writing my first play on a bread wrapper.” On Saturday, near the steps at Pier Beach, Rowan watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I wrote mine for my sister who hasn't entered a theater since the panic attacks began.
appearance: Rowan is easy to recognize by a long plait tucked inside the collar and one cheek that creases before the other. Usually dressed in a cropped bottle-green coat with a train token tied to a zipper pull, Rowan gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in when listening.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To perform the short play privately for the sister.
family: Ingrid Moss is Rowan’s stepsibling. Rowan puts the kettle on. Ingrid chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Home with stairs*, Ingrid says, “I deliver prescriptions here. I marked every landing where a person can set down a bag.”
connections: Clara Ferreira (drama tutor). They test whether a private scene works across a language difference.

reactions.situation: A young actor asks the listener to stop the pocket play
reactions.response: Rowan lets the actor stop without calling the audience's attention to the interruption.
